records.source: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις Ἁνανίας ὀνόματι σὺν Σαπφίρῃ τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπώλησεν κτῆμα καὶ ἐνοσφίσατο ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς, συνειδυίης καὶ τῆς γυναικός, καὶ ἐνέγκας μέρος τι παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων ἔθηκεν.
records.gloss: A man now certain Ananias by name with Sapphira the wife of him sold a property, \v 2 and he kept back from the price, being aware also the wife, and having brought a part certain at the feet of the apostles he laid [it].
pieces: A man called Ananias, however, sold a piece of land together with his wife Sapphira.
He secretly set aside some of the proceeds, and his wife knew of it. Then he brought the remaining portion and laid it at the apostles' feet.

L.1: Now a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a property,
L.2: and he kept back [some] of the price, his wife also knowing [of it], and bringing a certain part, he laid [it] at the feet of the apostles.

R.1: But there was a man named Ananias. He and his wife Sapphira sold some land.
R.2: Ananias kept part of the money for himself, and his wife knew about it. He brought the rest of the money and gave it to the apostles, as if it were all of it.

decisions.choice: now, but: a contrast with Barnabas just before
alternatives: a new story with no link
decisions.reason: 4:36-37 tells how Barnabas sold a field and laid all the money at the apostles' feet. Ananias does the same outwardly, but not honestly.

decisions.choice: kept back: the word used of Achan, who kept back what belonged to God
decisions.reason: The verb means to set aside for oneself, to pilfer (Titus 2:10). The Greek Old Testament uses it in Joshua 7:1, where Achan secretly took for himself what had been given over to God, at the start of Israel's life in the land. Here too sin threatens a new people of God at its start.

decisions.choice: his wife also knowing: she shared in the plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to know together with someone, to be in on it. 5:9 says they agreed together.

decisions.choice: laid it at the feet of the apostles: handed it over to the apostles' care
decisions.reason: The same act as in 4:35 and 4:37. The apostles gave out the money to anyone in need (4:35).

decisions.choice: as if it were all of it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the deception was. Peter's questions (5:3-4, 5:8) show that Ananias presented the part as the whole price.

records.heading: The lie of Ananias and Sapphira

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Ἁνανία, διὰ τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ Σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου, ψεύσασθαί σε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ νοσφίσασθαι ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου;
records.gloss: Said but the Peter, Ananias, why filled the Satan the heart of you, to lie you the Spirit the Holy and to keep back from the price of the land?
pieces: Peter said, "Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart, to make you lie to the Holy Spirit and keep part of the land's price back?

L.3: But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, [for] you to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep back [some] of the price of the land?

R.3: Peter said, "Ananias, why did you let Satan take control of your heart? You lied to the Holy Spirit. You kept some of the money from the land for yourself.

decisions.choice: Satan filled your heart: Satan took hold of his thinking and will
decisions.reason: Luke says Satan entered Judas (Luke 22:3). The believers have just been filled with the Holy Spirit (4:31); Ananias let another power fill him. Peter still holds him to account (5:4).

decisions.choice: to lie to the Holy Spirit: to lie to God
alternatives: to lie only to the apostles
decisions.reason: Peter says in 5:4 that Ananias lied to God. The Spirit was present in the community and its leaders, so lying to them was lying to the Spirit, and to God.

decisions.choice: keep back: the same verb as in 5:2
decisions.reason: He kept for himself part of what he claimed to have given.

decisions.choice: to lie: the result of Satan's filling
decisions.reason: The infinitive says what came of it: he lied and kept money back.

decisions.choice: why did you let Satan take control of your heart?
alternatives: why has Satan filled your heart?
decisions.reason: Readable puts Ananias's own part in the question, as 5:4 does ("why did you put this in your heart?").

records.source: οὐχὶ μένον σοὶ ἔμενεν καὶ πραθὲν ἐν τῇ σῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ὑπῆρχεν;
records.gloss: Not remaining to you was it remaining, and having been sold in the your authority was it?
pieces: Before it was sold, was it not your own? And after the sale, was the money not yours to use as you chose?

L.4: While it remained, did it not remain yours? And when it was sold, was it not in your authority?

R.4: The land belonged to you before you sold it. And after you sold it, you could do what you wanted with the money.

decisions.choice: two questions that expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: Peter is not asking for information. He is saying that the land and the money were Ananias's own.

decisions.choice: giving was free: the sin was the lie, not keeping the money
alternatives: everyone had to sell all they had
decisions.reason: The believers shared willingly (4:32-35). Ananias could have kept the land or the money. What he did wrong was to pretend.

decisions.choice: in your authority: under your control, yours to decide
decisions.reason: The word means power or right to act.

decisions.choice: two plain statements
decisions.reason: Readable states what Peter's questions imply.

records.source: τί ὅτι ἔθου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο;
records.gloss: Why [is it] that you put in the heart of you the deed this?
pieces: Why did you set your heart on doing this?

L.4: Why is it that you have put this deed in your heart?

R.4: Why did you decide to do this?

decisions.choice: put in your heart: decide, make up one's mind
decisions.reason: Luke 21:14 uses the same idiom: "settle it in your hearts".

decisions.choice: Satan filled his heart, yet he chose it
decisions.reason: Peter asked why Satan filled his heart (5:3); now he asks why Ananias himself planned it. Both are true.

records.source: οὐκ ἐψεύσω ἀνθρώποις ἀλλὰ τῷ θεῷ.
records.gloss: Not you lied to men but to the God.
pieces: It is not human beings you have lied to, but God."

L.4: You did not lie to {{gender:people|men}} but to God."

R.4: You did not lie to people. You lied to God!"

decisions.choice: not to people but to God: above all to God
alternatives: he had not lied to the apostles at all
decisions.reason: He did deceive the apostles. The "not ... but" form puts all the weight on the second part, as in Exodus 16:8, where Moses tells Israel their grumbling is "not against us but against the Lord".

decisions.choice: lying to the Holy Spirit (5:3) is lying to God
decisions.reason: Peter uses the two sayings of the same lie. The Spirit is God present with his people.

decisions.choice: people: human beings
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general, as against God.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, as the meaning note explains; Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive.

records.source: ἀκούων δὲ ὁ Ἁνανίας τοὺς λόγους τούτους πεσὼν ἐξέψυξεν· καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας.
records.gloss: Hearing now the Ananias the words these, having fallen he breathed out; and came fear great upon all those hearing.
pieces: As Ananias heard these words he fell down and died, and a great fear came over everyone who heard about it.

L.5: And Ananias, hearing these words, fell down and breathed his last; and great fear came upon all who heard [of it].

R.5: When Ananias heard this, he fell down dead. Everyone who heard about it was very afraid.

decisions.choice: breathed his last: died
decisions.reason: The verb means to breathe out one's life. Luke uses it again of Sapphira (5:10) and of Herod (12:23), each struck down by God.

decisions.choice: his death was God's judgment
decisions.reason: Peter pronounces no sentence on Ananias. His death follows at once on his lie to God (5:4), and the fear that follows is fear of God (5:11).

decisions.choice: all who heard: those present and those who heard the news later
decisions.reason: The present participle can cover both. 5:11 says the fear spread to all who heard of these things.

records.source: ἀναστάντες δὲ οἱ νεώτεροι συνέστειλαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν.
records.gloss: Having arisen then the younger [ones] wrapped up him and having carried out buried [him].
pieces: The young men stood up, wound him in a cloth, carried him out and buried him.

L.6: And the younger men got up, wrapped him up, and carrying [him] out, buried [him].

R.6: Some young men got up and wrapped his body in cloth. They carried him out and buried him.

decisions.choice: the younger men: young men of the community
decisions.reason: The word means simply the younger ones. 5:10 uses another word for young men. There is no sign of a set office.

decisions.choice: wrapped him up: covered or wound the body
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw together or wrap up, here preparing the body for burial.

decisions.choice: buried him: burial on the same day
decisions.reason: Jews usually buried the dead on the day they died, outside the city. Here it happens before his wife even knows (5:7).

decisions.choice: in a cloth (B); in cloth (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what he was wrapped in, as burial customs imply.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς ὡρῶν τριῶν διάστημα καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ μὴ εἰδυῖα τὸ γεγονὸς εἰσῆλθεν.
records.gloss: It came to pass now about hours three interval, and the wife of him not knowing the having happened came in.
pieces: Some three hours later his wife arrived, unaware of what had taken place.

L.7: And there was an interval of about three hours, and his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.

R.7: About three hours later, Ananias's wife came in. She did not know what had happened to her husband.

decisions.choice: not knowing: no one had told her
decisions.reason: She comes in without knowing her husband is dead, so Peter's question gives her a chance to tell the truth (5:8).

decisions.choice: came in: to where Peter and the believers were
decisions.reason: Peter is there to speak to her (5:8).

decisions.choice: to her husband
decisions.reason: Readable says whom it had happened to.

records.source: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν Πέτρος· Εἰπέ μοι, εἰ τοσούτου τὸ χωρίον ἀπέδοσθε;
records.gloss: Answered then to her Peter, Tell me, if for so much the land you sold?
pieces: Peter said to her, "Tell me, did the two of you sell the land for this amount?"

L.8: And Peter answered her, "Tell me whether you sold the land for so much."

R.8: Peter asked her, "Tell me, is this how much money you and your husband got for the land?"

decisions.choice: answered: spoke in response to her coming
decisions.reason: No one has asked anything. As in 3:12, the verb means he spoke up.

decisions.choice: you sold: you two, the plural
decisions.reason: The verb is plural. Peter asks about what she and Ananias did together.

decisions.choice: for so much: the sum Ananias had brought
decisions.reason: Peter likely points to the money laid at his feet, or names it. Either way she is asked to confirm the false price.

decisions.choice: the two of you (B); you and your husband (R)
decisions.reason: English "you" does not show the plural, so Balanced and Readable spell it out.

records.source: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, τοσούτου.
records.gloss: She and said, Yes, for so much.
pieces: "Yes," she replied, "that was the price."

L.8: And she said, "Yes, for so much."

R.8: She said, "Yes, that is how much."

decisions.choice: she repeats the lie in her own words
decisions.reason: Given the chance to speak the truth, she confirms the false price. Peter's next words (5:9) say they had agreed on it together.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς αὐτήν· Τί ὅτι συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν πειράσαι τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου;
records.gloss: The but Peter [said] to her, Why that it was agreed by you to test the Spirit of Lord?
pieces: Peter said to her, "Why did the two of you agree together to put the Spirit of the Lord to the test?

L.9: And Peter [said] to her, "Why is it that you agreed together to test the Spirit of [the] Lord?

R.9: Then Peter said to her, "Why did you and your husband plan together to test the Lord's Spirit like this?

decisions.choice: to test: to try God's patience, as Israel did in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Israel tested God at Massah (Exodus 17:2, 17:7), and the law says, "You shall not put the Lord your God to the test" (Deuteronomy 6:16; Luke 4:12). Ananias and Sapphira acted as if the Spirit would not see.

decisions.choice: agreed together: made a shared plan
decisions.reason: The verb means to sound together, to come to an agreement. It confirms 5:2.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of the Lord: the Holy Spirit of 5:3
decisions.reason: The Lord may be God, as in Luke 4:18, which quotes Isaiah, or the Lord Jesus, as in 16:7, where the Spirit is called "the Spirit of Jesus". The Spirit is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the two of you (B); you and your husband (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8, English needs to show the plural.

records.source: ἰδοὺ οἱ πόδες τῶν θαψάντων τὸν ἄνδρα σου ἐπὶ τῇ θύρᾳ καὶ ἐξοίσουσίν σε.
records.gloss: Behold the feet of those having buried the husband of you [are] at the door, and they will carry out you.
pieces: Look, the men who buried your husband are already at the door. They will carry you out as well."

L.9: Look, the feet of those who buried your husband [are] at the door, and they will carry you out."

R.9: The men who just buried your husband are at the door. They will carry you out too."

decisions.choice: the feet are at the door: they are arriving now
alternatives: only their footsteps can be heard
decisions.reason: "Feet" stands for the people coming. They are just back from the burial, about three hours after it began (5:7).

decisions.choice: they will carry you out: Peter foretells her death
alternatives: a threat of punishment by the believers
decisions.reason: Peter speaks as a prophet. He does not strike her down; he says what God will do, and it happens at once (5:10).

decisions.choice: the men who buried your husband are at the door
alternatives: the feet of those who buried
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps "feet".

records.source: ἔπεσεν δὲ παραχρῆμα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξέψυξεν· εἰσελθόντες δὲ οἱ νεανίσκοι εὗρον αὐτὴν νεκράν, καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: She fell then at once at the feet of him and breathed out; having come in then the young men found her dead, and having carried out they buried [her] beside the husband of her.
pieces: Instantly she collapsed at Peter's feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, and carried her out to bury her next to her husband.

L.10: And immediately she fell down at his feet and breathed her last; and the young men came in and found her dead, and carrying [her] out, they buried [her] beside her husband.

R.10: Right away she fell down at Peter's feet and died. The young men came in and saw that she was dead. They carried her out and buried her beside her husband.

decisions.choice: at his feet: where the money had been laid
decisions.reason: The gift was laid "at the feet of the apostles" (5:2); now she falls at Peter's feet. Luke tells it so that the two scenes answer each other.

decisions.choice: breathed her last: died
decisions.reason: The same verb as of Ananias (5:5).

decisions.choice: the young men: the same group as in 5:6
decisions.reason: Luke uses a different word, but they are the younger men who buried Ananias.

decisions.choice: Peter's feet
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Peter.

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας ταῦτα.
records.gloss: And came fear great upon whole the church and upon all those hearing these things.
pieces: The entire church was filled with deep fear, as was everyone who heard about these things.

L.11: And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.

R.11: All the believers in the church were very afraid. So was everyone else who heard about what had happened.

decisions.choice: the church: the community of those who believe in Jesus, God's people gathered together
decisions.reason: This is the word's first use in Acts. It means an assembly of people called together. The Greek Old Testament uses it for Israel gathered before God (Deuteronomy 4:10, 31:30), and Stephen uses it so of Israel in the wilderness (7:38). In 19:32-41 it is a town's assembly. Here it names the believers as one body (8:1, 9:31). It means people, not a building.

decisions.choice: fear: dread and awe of God
decisions.reason: As in 2:43 and 9:31, the fear is a deep reverence for God, who had shown that he could not be deceived.

decisions.choice: all who heard: those outside the church as well
decisions.reason: "And upon all" adds people beyond the church. 5:13 shows the effect on outsiders.

decisions.choice: church
decisions.reason: "Church" is the English word for this community of believers, as the meaning note explains. "Assembly" is kept for the places where the word means another gathering (7:38, 19:32-41).

decisions.choice: all the believers in the church
decisions.reason: Readable says that the church is the believers.

records.source: Διὰ δὲ τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πολλὰ ἐν τῷ λαῷ· καὶ ἦσαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἅπαντες ἐν τῇ Στοᾷ Σολομῶντος·
records.gloss: Through now the hands of the apostles were happening signs and wonders many among the people; and they were with one accord all in the Porch of Solomon,
pieces: By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders kept taking place among the people. With one mind, the believers all gathered in Solomon's Porch.

L.12: And through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were happening among the people; and they were all with one mind in Solomon's Porch.

R.12: God used the apostles to do many signs and wonders among the people. All the believers met together at Solomon's Porch, a covered walkway in the temple courts.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: astonishing works that point to God
decisions.reason: The believers had prayed for this in 4:30. The same pair describes the works of Jesus (2:22) and of the apostles (2:43).

decisions.choice: through the hands of the apostles: God working through them
alternatives: only by laying on of hands
decisions.reason: "Hands" stands for what a person does. The believers asked God to stretch out his hand to heal (4:30).

decisions.choice: they all: the believers, or the apostles
decisions.reason: The last people named are the apostles. But "all" and "with one mind" are used of the whole community (2:46, 4:24), and 5:13 contrasts them with "the rest".

decisions.choice: Solomon's Porch: the roofed colonnade on the east side of the temple's outer court
decisions.reason: As in 3:11.

decisions.choice: God used the apostles to do
alternatives: through the hands of the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one at work, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" most likely are, as the meaning note explains.

records.heading: Signs and wonders among the people

records.source: τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν οὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα κολλᾶσθαι αὐτοῖς, ἀλλ’ ἐμεγάλυνεν αὐτοὺς ὁ λαός, μᾶλλον δὲ προσετίθεντο πιστεύοντες τῷ κυρίῳ πλήθη ἀνδρῶν τε καὶ γυναικῶν·
records.gloss: Of the but rest no one was daring to join them, but were magnifying them the people; \v 14 more and were being added believing to the Lord, multitudes of men both and of women,
pieces: None of the others dared to associate with them, yet the people thought highly of them.
Still more believers were brought to the Lord, great numbers of men and women alike.

L.13: But of the rest no one dared to join them, but the people held them in high honor;
L.14: and more than ever believers were added to the Lord, crowds of both men and women,

R.13: Other people were afraid to join the believers, but everyone spoke well of them.
R.14: More and more people believed and became followers of the Lord. Many men and many women joined them.

decisions.choice: the rest: people outside the believers
alternatives: the rest of the believers, who kept apart from the apostles
decisions.reason: After what happened to Ananias and Sapphira, no one joined the believers lightly. Yet many did join who truly believed (5:14). Some read "the rest" as other believers who held back from the apostles.

decisions.choice: join: to attach oneself closely to a group
decisions.reason: The verb means to be glued or joined to. 9:26 and 10:28 use it for associating with people.

decisions.choice: held them in high honor: praised them
decisions.reason: The verb means to make great, so to speak highly of.

decisions.choice: added to the Lord: brought into the Lord's people by believing
alternatives: believing in the Lord, they were added (to the church)
decisions.reason: The words "to the Lord" can go with "were added" or with "believing". 11:24 says a great crowd "was added to the Lord", and 2:47 says the Lord added to their number. Either way, they believed in the Lord and joined his people.

decisions.choice: both men and women: Luke names both
decisions.reason: Luke often names women alongside men among the believers (8:3, 8:12, 17:4, 17:12).

decisions.choice: believed and became followers of the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says what being added to the Lord means.

records.source: ὥστε καὶ εἰς τὰς πλατείας ἐκφέρειν τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς καὶ τιθέναι ἐπὶ κλιναρίων καὶ κραβάττων, ἵνα ἐρχομένου Πέτρου κἂν ἡ σκιὰ ἐπισκιάσῃ τινὶ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: so that even into the streets to carry out the sick and to put on cots and mats, so that coming Peter at least the shadow might overshadow some of them.
pieces: People would even carry their sick out into the streets and lay them on cots and pallets, hoping that when Peter came along, his shadow, if nothing more, might fall across some of them.

L.15: so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid [them] on cots and mats, so that when Peter came by, at least [his] shadow might fall on some of them.

R.15: People even carried sick people out into the streets. They put them on beds and mats. They hoped that when Peter walked by, his shadow would at least touch some of them.

decisions.choice: so that: the result of the signs in 5:12
decisions.reason: 5:12b-14 is an aside about the believers; "so that" picks up the signs done by the apostles. It may also follow from the growth just described.

decisions.choice: cots and mats: beds that could be carried
decisions.reason: The first word is a small bed; the second is a poor person's mat or pallet, as in Mark 2:4.

decisions.choice: his shadow at least: the people's hope of healing
decisions.reason: Luke reports what people hoped, as with the woman who touched Jesus's clothes (Luke 8:44) and the cloths taken from Paul (19:12). 5:16 says that all were healed, so God honored their faith.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the sentence ends here
alternatives: some manuscripts add "and they were set free from every sickness they had"
decisions.reason: Codex Bezae and some other witnesses add words saying the sick were freed from their illnesses. The SBLGNT, with most manuscripts, does not have them. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: if nothing more
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "at least" in a way that reads naturally after "his shadow".

records.source: συνήρχετο δὲ καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πέριξ πόλεων Ἰερουσαλήμ, φέροντες ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ὀχλουμένους ὑπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων, οἵτινες ἐθεραπεύοντο ἅπαντες.
records.gloss: Were coming together now also the multitude of the around cities of Jerusalem, bringing sick and being troubled by spirits unclean, who were being healed all.
pieces: People streamed in, too, from the towns near Jerusalem. They brought those who were sick or harassed by unclean spirits, and every one of them was made well.

L.16: And the crowd from the towns around Jerusalem also came together, bringing [the] sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, who were all healed.

R.16: Large crowds also came from the towns around Jerusalem. They brought people who were sick and people who were troubled by evil spirits. And all of them were healed.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the towns around Jerusalem"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "the towns around, to Jerusalem"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("the cities round about unto Jerusalem"), add "to", so that the crowds come into Jerusalem. The meaning is close. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: unclean spirits: demons
decisions.reason: Luke uses this name for demons (Luke 4:33, 4:36, 8:29). Those troubled by them are named apart from the sick.

decisions.choice: all were healed: no one went away unhealed
decisions.reason: As with Jesus (Luke 4:40, 6:19). The healing is God's doing (4:30).

decisions.choice: evil spirits
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plainer word for spirits that are against God.

records.source: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ πάντες οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ, ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου καὶ ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ ἔθεντο αὐτοὺς ἐν τηρήσει δημοσίᾳ.
records.gloss: Having risen up but the high priest and all those with him, the being sect of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy \v 18 and laid the hands on the apostles and put them in custody public.
pieces: But the high priest rose to act, and with him all who sided with him, the Sadducee party. Burning with jealousy,
they took hold of the apostles and shut them up in the public prison.

L.17: But the high priest rose up, and all those with him, that is, the party of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy,
L.18: and they laid hands on the apostles and put them in [the] public jail.

R.17: The high priest and his friends, the Sadducees, became very jealous of the apostles. So they decided to act.
R.18: They arrested the apostles and put them in the city jail.

decisions.choice: rose up: took action
decisions.reason: The verb is used of someone setting out to do something, as in 5:34 and 5:36.

decisions.choice: the high priest: the head of the temple and of the council
decisions.reason: Caiaphas held the office in these years; Luke also calls his father-in-law Annas high priest (4:6; Luke 3:2; John 18:13). Which one is meant here is not said.

decisions.choice: the party of the Sadducees: a group of leading priestly families
alternatives: a sect cut off from Judaism
decisions.reason: The Sadducees held the high priesthood and much power in the temple. They said there is no resurrection, no angel and no spirit (23:8; Luke 20:27). They were angry that the apostles proclaimed the resurrection in Jesus (4:1-2). "Party" has no bad sense here; Luke uses the same word of the Pharisees (15:5).

decisions.choice: jealousy: resentment at the apostles' success
decisions.reason: The word can mean zeal, but here, as in 13:45, it is jealousy at the crowds who honored the apostles (5:13-16).

decisions.choice: the public jail: the city's prison
decisions.reason: A jail kept by the authorities, as in 4:3. All the apostles were held this time, not just Peter and John.

decisions.choice: jealous of the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they were jealous of.

records.heading: An angel opens the prison doors

records.source: ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου διὰ νυκτὸς ἤνοιξε τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς ἐξαγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἶπεν·
records.gloss: An angel but of Lord during night opened the doors of the prison, having brought out and them said,
pieces: That night, though, an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison. He led them outside and said to them,

L.19: But during the night an angel of [the] Lord opened the doors of the prison, and bringing them out, he said,

R.19: But that night an angel from the Lord opened the doors of the jail. He led the apostles out and said to them,

decisions.choice: an angel of the Lord: a messenger sent by God
decisions.reason: Angels of the Lord appear in Luke 1:11 and 2:9, and one frees Peter in 12:7-10. The Sadducees, who jailed the apostles, said there are no angels (23:8).

decisions.choice: during the night: in the course of that night
decisions.reason: The apostles were seized in the day and freed that same night; they are in the temple at dawn (5:21).

decisions.choice: the apostles
decisions.reason: Readable names them.

records.source: Πορεύεσθε καὶ σταθέντες λαλεῖτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τῷ λαῷ πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τῆς ζωῆς ταύτης.
records.gloss: Go and having stood speak in the temple to the people all the words of the life this.
pieces: "Go and take your stand in the temple, and tell the people the whole message of this life."

L.20: "Go, and standing in the temple, speak to the people all the words of this life."

R.20: "Go to the temple. Stand there and tell the people everything about the life that Jesus gives."

decisions.choice: the words of this life: the message of the life that comes through Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter has called Jesus the Author of life (3:15). In 13:26 Paul speaks of "the message of this salvation". "This life" is the life the apostles proclaim, the life the Sadducees deny.

decisions.choice: standing: take your place openly
decisions.reason: They are to stand up in public, in the very place they were arrested from. 5:25 reports them "standing" there.

decisions.choice: the temple: the temple courts, where people gathered
decisions.reason: As in 2:46 and 3:1.

decisions.choice: the life that Jesus gives
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this life" is, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἰσῆλθον ὑπὸ τὸν ὄρθρον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκον.
records.gloss: Having heard now they entered at the dawn into the temple and were teaching.
pieces: Hearing this, they went into the temple at first light and began to teach.

L.21: And having heard [this], they went into the temple about daybreak and began teaching.

R.21: The apostles obeyed. Early the next morning they went into the temple courts and started teaching.

decisions.choice: having heard: they did as the angel said
decisions.reason: They obeyed at once, as early in the day as they could.

decisions.choice: about daybreak: when the temple opened and people began to come
decisions.reason: The morning sacrifice was offered at dawn, and people came early to the temple courts (Luke 21:38).

decisions.choice: the apostles obeyed
decisions.reason: Readable says what their hearing led to.

records.source: Παραγενόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ συνεκάλεσαν τὸ συνέδριον καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον ἀχθῆναι αὐτούς.
records.gloss: Having arrived now the high priest and those with him called together the council and all the senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to be brought them.
pieces: Meanwhile the high priest and his party arrived. They summoned the council together with all the elders of Israel, and sent orders to the prison to bring the apostles.

L.21: Now the high priest and those with him came and called together the council and all the senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.

R.21: Meanwhile the high priest and his friends called together the council and all the elders of Israel. The council was the group of Jewish leaders who governed the people. Then they sent men to the jail to bring the apostles to them.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin, the Jewish high council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: It was made up of chief priests, elders and scribes, with the high priest presiding (4:5-6; Luke 22:66). Later Jewish writings give it seventy-one members. Under Roman rule it governed Jewish affairs.

decisions.choice: and all the senate: the council's own body of elders, or elders added to it
decisions.reason: "And" may explain the council, "that is, the whole senate", or add to it other respected elders. The Greek Old Testament speaks of "the senate of the sons of Israel" (Exodus 12:21). Either way, Luke stresses that the full leadership of Israel was there.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: An old name for the nation, as in Exodus.

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel
alternatives: the senate of the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the senate was and use the plain name of the people; Literal keeps both words.

decisions.choice: the group of Jewish leaders who governed the people
decisions.reason: Readable says what the council was.

records.source: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι ὑπηρέται οὐχ εὗρον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ, ἀναστρέψαντες δὲ ἀπήγγειλαν λέγοντες ὅτι Τὸ δεσμωτήριον εὕρομεν κεκλεισμένον ἐν πάσῃ ἀσφαλείᾳ καὶ τοὺς φύλακας ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τῶν θυρῶν, ἀνοίξαντες δὲ ἔσω οὐδένα εὕρομεν.
records.gloss: The but having arrived officers not found them in the prison; having returned then they reported \v 23 saying that, The prison we found shut with all security and the guards standing at the doors, having opened but inside no one we found.
pieces: The officers went, but they did not find the apostles in the prison. They came back with this report:
"The prison was shut and fully secured when we got there, and the guards were at their posts by the doors. But once we had opened up, we found nobody inside."

L.22: But the officers who came did not find them in the prison, and they returned and reported,
L.23: saying, "We found the prison shut with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened [them], we found no one inside."

R.22: The men went to the jail, but the apostles were not there. So they went back and told the leaders,
R.23: "The jail was locked tight, and the guards were standing at the doors. But when we opened the doors, nobody was inside!"

decisions.choice: the officers: the temple police, under the captain of the temple
decisions.reason: The word means attendants or officers. They serve the captain of the temple (5:26).

decisions.choice: locked and guarded, yet empty
decisions.reason: Everything was secure, and no one had seen anything. The report shows that the apostles were freed by God, not by a human plan.

decisions.choice: with all security: locked as firmly as it could be
decisions.reason: The phrase means fully secured.

decisions.choice: the apostles; the leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people the pronouns point to.

records.source: ὡς δὲ ἤκουσαν τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὅ τε στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, διηπόρουν περὶ αὐτῶν τί ἂν γένοιτο τοῦτο.
records.gloss: As now they heard the words these, both the captain of the temple and the chief priests were perplexed about them, what might become this.
pieces: The report left the captain of the temple and the chief priests puzzled about the apostles, unsure what all this would come to.

L.24: And when they heard these words, both the captain of the temple and the chief priests were at a loss about them, [as to] what this might come to.

R.24: The captain of the temple guard and the leading priests heard this. They could not understand what had happened to the apostles. They wondered what would happen next.

decisions.choice: the captain of the temple: the priest in charge of the temple police
decisions.reason: He kept order in the temple with his officers (4:1; Luke 22:4, 22:52). He ranked next to the high priest among the temple leaders.

decisions.choice: the chief priests: the high priest's family and the leading priests
decisions.reason: As in 4:6 and 4:23, those of the high-priestly families who led the temple.

decisions.choice: about them: about the apostles, or about these words
decisions.reason: The pronoun is plural and may point to the apostles or to the reports. The sense is the same: they could not explain what had happened.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the captain of the temple and the chief priests"
alternatives: many manuscripts add "the high priest" (or "the priest") at the start
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "the high priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the captain of the temple guard; the leading priests
alternatives: the captain of the temple; the chief priests
decisions.reason: Readable says what the captain was in charge of, and uses a plainer word for "chief".

records.source: παραγενόμενος δέ τις ἀπήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οὓς ἔθεσθε ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ εἰσὶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστῶτες καὶ διδάσκοντες τὸν λαόν.
records.gloss: Having arrived then someone reported to them that, Behold the men whom you put in the prison are in the temple standing and teaching the people.
pieces: Then a man arrived with news for them: "Those men you locked up are in the temple right now, standing there teaching the people!"

L.25: Then someone came and reported to them, "Look, the men whom you put in the prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people."

R.25: Then someone came and said to them, "Listen! The men you put in jail are in the temple courts. They are standing there, teaching the people!"

decisions.choice: standing: openly, just as the angel told them
decisions.reason: The angel said, "Go and stand in the temple" (5:20); they did exactly that.

decisions.choice: look: a word to draw attention
decisions.reason: The word calls for attention to something surprising.

decisions.choice: right now, with an exclamation
decisions.reason: Balanced conveys the surprise without an archaic "behold".

records.source: τότε ἀπελθὼν ὁ στρατηγὸς σὺν τοῖς ὑπηρέταις ἤγαγεν αὐτούς, οὐ μετὰ βίας, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν, μὴ λιθασθῶσιν.
records.gloss: Then having gone the captain with the officers brought them, not with force, they were fearing for the people lest they be stoned.
pieces: The captain then went with his officers and fetched the apostles. They used no violence, for they were afraid of the crowd and of being stoned.

L.26: Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, not with force, for they feared the people, lest they be stoned.

R.26: So the captain and his men went and brought the apostles back. But they did not hurt them or force them to come. They were afraid that the people would throw stones at them.

decisions.choice: lest they be stoned: the officers feared being stoned by the people
decisions.reason: "They" are the captain and his officers. The people honored the apostles (5:13), and a crowd might have turned on anyone who mistreated them.

decisions.choice: stoned: killed or attacked with stones by a crowd
decisions.reason: Stoning was the law's penalty for some crimes (Leviticus 24:16), but crowds also used it in anger (14:19; Luke 20:6).

decisions.choice: not with force: without violence
decisions.reason: They brought them back without seizing them roughly.

decisions.choice: throw stones at them
decisions.reason: Readable says what stoning was.

records.source: Ἀγαγόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔστησαν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ.
records.gloss: Having brought then them they stood [them] in the council.
pieces: They brought them in and stood them before the council.

L.27: And having brought them, they stood [them] in the council.

R.27: They brought the apostles in and made them stand in front of the council.

decisions.choice: stood them in the council: brought them to trial
decisions.reason: The accused stood before the council, as Peter and John did in 4:7.

records.heading: Obeying God rather than people

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς λέγων· Παραγγελίᾳ παρηγγείλαμεν ὑμῖν μὴ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πεπληρώκατε τὴν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῆς διδαχῆς ὑμῶν, καὶ βούλεσθε ἐπαγαγεῖν ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου.
records.gloss: And asked them the high priest \v 28 saying, With a charge we charged you not to teach in the name this, and behold you have filled the Jerusalem with the teaching of you, and you intend to bring upon us the blood of the man this.
pieces: The high priest began to question them:
"We ordered you in no uncertain terms to stop teaching in this name. Now look: your teaching has spread all through Jerusalem, and you are set on laying this man's blood at our door."

L.27: And the high priest questioned them,
L.28: saying, "We strictly charged you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring the blood of this man upon us."

R.28: He said, "We told you clearly that you must not teach about this man. But you have spread your teaching all over Jerusalem! And you want people to blame us for his death."

decisions.choice: we charged you with a charge: we gave you strict orders
alternatives: we charged you with a crime
decisions.reason: Repeating the verb with its own noun makes it emphatic, as in Luke 22:15, "with desire I have desired". The order is the one given in 4:17-18.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: a statement, "We strictly charged you"
alternatives: many manuscripts add "not", making it a question: "Did we not strictly charge you?"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read it as a question. Others, some of them early, have the statement. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: this name; this man: the high priest avoids saying "Jesus"
decisions.reason: He speaks of Jesus without naming him. The apostles name him plainly (5:30).

decisions.choice: bring this man's blood upon us: make us guilty of his death
alternatives: bring a curse of bloodshed upon us
decisions.reason: "Blood on" someone means guilt for a death (2 Samuel 1:16; Matthew 27:25). The apostles have said the leaders killed Jesus (4:10).

decisions.choice: laying this man's blood at our door (B); blame us for his death (R)
alternatives: bring this man's blood upon us
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an English idiom with the same sense; Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: teach about this man
decisions.reason: Readable says what teaching "in this name" meant: teaching about Jesus by his authority.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι εἶπαν· Πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις.
records.gloss: Answering but Peter and the apostles said, To obey it is necessary God rather than men.
pieces: Peter and the other apostles replied, "It is God we must obey rather than people.

L.29: But Peter and the apostles answered and said, "[We] must obey God rather than {{gender:people|men}}.

R.29: Peter and the other apostles answered, "We have to do what God says, not what people say.

decisions.choice: obey: to obey one who has authority
decisions.reason: The verb is used of obeying a ruler. They own the council's authority, but God's comes first. The same verb comes in 5:32.

decisions.choice: obey God rather than people: what Peter and John said in 4:19
decisions.reason: They had told the council the same before (4:19-20).

decisions.choice: Peter and the apostles: Peter speaks for them all
decisions.reason: Peter is their spokesman, as in 2:14.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, as against God
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 5:4.

decisions.choice: the other apostles
decisions.reason: Peter is himself an apostle.

records.source: ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἤγειρεν Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ὑμεῖς διεχειρίσασθε κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου·
records.gloss: The God of the fathers of us raised Jesus, whom you killed having hanged on a tree.
pieces: The God of our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} raised Jesus, whom you had done away with by hanging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on a tree.

L.30: The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] on a tree.

R.30: The God our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} worshiped brought Jesus back to life. You had killed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by nailing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross.

decisions.choice: raised: raised from the dead
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for raising the dead (3:15, 10:40, 13:30), set against "whom you killed". It can also mean raising up a leader (13:22), and some read it so here.

decisions.choice: hanging him on a tree: the cross, as the law speaks of one hanged on a tree
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 21:22-23 says that one hanged on a tree is under God's curse. Peter uses the same words in 10:39, and Paul in 13:29 and Galatians 3:13. The leaders meant the cross as a curse; God raised him.

decisions.choice: killed: laid violent hands on, murdered
decisions.reason: The verb means to kill with one's own hands (26:21).

decisions.choice: our fathers: our forebears
decisions.reason: The forebears of Israel, as in 3:13.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 3:13; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: brought back to life; nailing him to a cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what the words refer to, as the meaning notes explain.

records.source: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἀρχηγὸν καὶ σωτῆρα ὕψωσεν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ δοῦναι μετάνοιαν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·
records.gloss: This one the God Leader and Savior exalted to the right hand of him, to give repentance to the Israel and forgiveness of sins.
pieces: He is the one God has lifted up to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand as Leader and Savior, to grant Israel repentance and forgiveness of sins.

L.31: This one God exalted to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand [as] Leader and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.

R.31: God lifted Jesus up to the place of honor at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right side. God made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Leader and Savior. He did this so that the people of Israel could be given a change of heart and have their sins forgiven.

decisions.choice: Leader: the one who goes first and leads his people
decisions.reason: The word means a leader or founder. In 3:15 it is "the Author of life". Here, paired with "Savior", the sense of leader and ruler comes forward.

decisions.choice: to his right hand: lifted to the place beside God
decisions.reason: As in 2:33, the form can mean "to" or "by".

decisions.choice: Savior: a title of God, now given to Jesus
decisions.reason: God is called Savior in Isaiah 45:21 and Luke 1:47; Jesus in Luke 2:11 and Acts 13:23.

decisions.choice: to give repentance: repentance itself is God's gift
decisions.reason: In 11:18 the believers say God has given repentance to the nations too. The giver may be God or the exalted Jesus; the sentence does not say which.

decisions.choice: a change of heart
decisions.reason: Readable says what repentance is, in plain words.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the Greek sentence into steps, naming Jesus.

records.source: καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες τῶν ῥημάτων τούτων, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ὃ ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς τοῖς πειθαρχοῦσιν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And we are witnesses of the things these, and the Spirit the Holy whom gave the God to those obeying him.
pieces: We ourselves testify to these things, and so does the Holy Spirit, given by God to all who obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.32: And we are witnesses of these things, and [so is] the Holy Spirit, whom God gave to those obeying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.32: We saw these things happen, and we tell people about them. The Holy Spirit also shows that they are true. God has given the Spirit to everyone who obeys {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: these things: the events Peter has named
decisions.reason: The word can mean words or matters. Here it means the death, raising and exaltation of Jesus (5:30-31), as in Luke 2:15.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit is also a witness
alternatives: the Spirit only helps the apostles
decisions.reason: Jesus said the Spirit would testify about him, and so would his followers (John 15:26-27; Acts 1:8). The signs and the gift of the Spirit back up the apostles' words.

decisions.choice: those who obey him: the same verb as in 5:29
decisions.reason: The apostles obey God; the Spirit is given to all who do. The council is implicitly invited to obey as well.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "we are witnesses"
alternatives: some manuscripts read "we are his witnesses"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("we are his witnesses of these things"), add a word meaning "his" or "in him". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: we saw these things happen, and we tell people about them; shows that they are true
alternatives: we are witnesses; and the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what being a witness means, and what the Spirit's witness is, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες διεπρίοντο καὶ ἐβούλοντο ἀνελεῖν αὐτούς.
records.gloss: Those but having heard were being sawn through and were wanting to kill them.
pieces: Hearing this, the council members were enraged and were ready to have the apostles killed.

L.33: And when they heard [this], they were cut to the quick and wanted to kill them.

R.33: When the council members heard this, they became very angry. They wanted to kill the apostles.

decisions.choice: cut to the quick: furious
decisions.reason: The verb means to be sawn through. In 7:54 it is used again of rage. The crowd at Pentecost was "pierced to the heart" and repented (2:37); these hearers are torn by anger instead.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "they wanted"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("took counsel to slay them"), have a similar verb meaning "they were planning". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the council members; the apostles
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people.

records.heading: Gamaliel's counsel

records.source: ἀναστὰς δέ τις ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ Φαρισαῖος ὀνόματι Γαμαλιήλ, νομοδιδάσκαλος τίμιος παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, ἐκέλευσεν ἔξω βραχὺ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ποιῆσαι, εἶπέν τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις τί μέλλετε πράσσειν.
records.gloss: Having risen up but a certain one in the council Pharisee by name Gamaliel, teacher of the law honored by all the people, commanded outside briefly the men to put, \v 35 said and to them, Men Israelites, take heed to yourselves concerning the men these what you are about to do.
pieces: But one of the council stood up, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law respected by the whole people. He had the men sent outside for a short time,
and then he spoke to the council: "Men of Israel, be careful how you deal with these men.

L.34: But a certain Pharisee in the council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law honored by all the people, stood up and ordered the men to be put outside for a short while,
L.35: and he said to them, "Men, Israelites, take heed to yourselves as to what you are about to do to these men.

R.34: But one of the council members stood up. He was a Pharisee named Gamaliel. He was a teacher of God's law, and all the people respected him. He told the guards to take the apostles outside for a short time.
R.35: Then he said to the council, "Men of Israel, be careful about what you are planning to do to these men.

decisions.choice: a Pharisee: one of the party known for careful keeping of the law
decisions.reason: The Pharisees kept the law and the traditions of the elders strictly. Unlike the Sadducees, they believed in the resurrection and in angels (23:6-8).

decisions.choice: Gamaliel: a leading teacher of the law in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Paul was taught by him (22:3). Later Jewish tradition remembered him with great honor as Rabban Gamaliel the Elder (Mishnah Sotah 9:15).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the men"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have "the apostles". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: men, Israelites: a formal address to the council
decisions.reason: The same formal address as 2:22 and 3:12, but here it is spoken to the council, whose members were all men. So it is not widened to men and women.

decisions.choice: take heed to yourselves: be careful, for your own sake
decisions.reason: A warning (20:28; Luke 17:3). Gamaliel warns them that they themselves may be at risk (5:39).

decisions.choice: told the guards to take the apostles outside
alternatives: ordered the men to be put outside
decisions.reason: Readable names who did it and who was taken out.

records.source: πρὸ γὰρ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀνέστη Θευδᾶς, λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτόν, ᾧ προσεκλίθη ἀνδρῶν ἀριθμὸς ὡς τετρακοσίων· ὃς ἀνῃρέθη, καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διελύθησαν καὶ ἐγένοντο εἰς οὐδέν.
records.gloss: Before for these the days rose up Theudas, saying to be somebody himself, to whom were joined of men a number about four hundred; who was killed, and all as many as were obeying him were dispersed and came to nothing.
pieces: In days gone by Theudas came forward, making himself out to be someone great, and around 400 men took his side. He was killed, those who had followed his lead were broken up, and nothing was left of it.

L.36: For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming himself to be somebody, to whom a number of men, about 400, joined themselves; he was killed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing.

R.36: Some time ago a man named Theudas came along. He said he was someone important, and about 400 men joined him. But he was killed. All his followers were scattered, and nothing came of it.

decisions.choice: Theudas: the leader of a movement before Judas the Galilean, otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: The historian Josephus (Antiquities 20.97-98) tells of a Theudas who claimed to be a prophet and was killed under the governor Fadus, about AD 44-46. That is some ten years after Gamaliel's speech, and long after Judas (AD 6), whom Gamaliel places after Theudas. Gamaliel may mean an earlier leader of the same name; Josephus describes many uprisings after Herod the Great died in 4 BC. The question is not settled.

decisions.choice: claiming to be somebody: claiming to be someone important
decisions.reason: He set himself up as a leader, perhaps as a prophet or a deliverer.

decisions.choice: followed him: were persuaded by him, obeyed him
decisions.reason: The verb means to be persuaded, and so to follow.

decisions.choice: came to nothing: the movement ended with its leader
decisions.reason: This is Gamaliel's point: a movement of merely human origin dies with its leader.

records.source: μετὰ τοῦτον ἀνέστη Ἰούδας ὁ Γαλιλαῖος ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς ἀπογραφῆς καὶ ἀπέστησε λαὸν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ· κἀκεῖνος ἀπώλετο καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διεσκορπίσθησαν.
records.gloss: After this one rose up Judas the Galilean in the days of the census and drew away people after him; and that one perished, and all as many as were obeying him were scattered.
pieces: After him came Judas the Galilean, at the time of the census, who drew a following of people after him. He also perished, and those who had followed his lead were all scattered abroad.

L.37: After this man Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew away people after him; he too perished, and all who followed him were scattered.

R.37: After that, at the time when the Romans counted the people, Judas from Galilee came along. He got people to follow him. But he died too, and his followers were scattered.

decisions.choice: Judas the Galilean: the leader of a revolt against Roman rule
decisions.reason: Josephus (Antiquities 18.1-10; Jewish War 2.118) tells how Judas of Galilee urged the Jews to resist the Roman census and not to pay tribute to Rome, saying God alone was their master.

decisions.choice: the census: the Roman registration of people and property for taxes
decisions.reason: Josephus dates it to AD 6, when Judea came under direct Roman rule and Quirinius, governor of Syria, carried out a registration. Luke 2:2 also speaks of a registration under Quirinius.

decisions.choice: drew away people after him: led people into revolt
decisions.reason: The verb means to draw away, here from loyalty to the rulers.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "people"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "many people" or "much people"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("much people"), add a word for many. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the time when the Romans counted the people
decisions.reason: Readable says what the census was.

records.source: καὶ τὰ νῦν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπόστητε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τούτων καὶ ἄφετε αὐτούς· ὅτι ἐὰν ᾖ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἡ βουλὴ αὕτη ἢ τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο, καταλυθήσεται, εἰ δὲ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐστιν, οὐ δυνήσεσθε καταλῦσαι αὐτούς· μήποτε καὶ θεομάχοι εὑρεθῆτε.
records.gloss: And the now I say to you, stand away from the men these and let go them; because if it is from men the plan this or the work this, it will be overthrown, \v 39 if but from God it is, not you will be able to overthrow them, lest even fighters against God you be found.
pieces: So here is what I say to you now: keep clear of these men and let them be. If this plan or this work has a human source, it will fall apart,
but if it comes from God, you will not be able to bring them down. You may even turn out to be at war with God."

L.38: And now I say to you, keep away from these men and let them go, because if this plan or this work is from {{gender:people|men}}, it will be overthrown;
L.39: but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them, lest you even be found [to be] fighting against God."

R.38: So here is what I tell you. Stay away from these men, and do not do anything to them. If this plan or work comes from people, it will fail.
R.39: But if it comes from God, you will not be able to destroy them. You might even find out that you are fighting against God!"

decisions.choice: two different forms of "if"
decisions.reason: The first "if" uses a form often used of what may or may not happen; the second uses a form that can take the case as real for the argument. Some read this as Gamaliel leaning toward the second, that the movement is from God. But writers of the time did not always keep the difference, and Gamaliel may simply be cautious.

decisions.choice: lest you be found fighting God: the reason to keep away
decisions.reason: The clause goes back to "keep away from these men" (5:38): leave them alone, so that you are not found fighting against God.

decisions.choice: fighting against God: opponents of God
decisions.reason: One word in the Greek, made of "God" and "fighter".

decisions.choice: from people: of human origin
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, as against God.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "overthrow them"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version ("ye cannot overthrow it"), have "it", the plan or work. Codex Bezae also adds a longer saying here. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As at 5:4; Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: do not do anything to them
decisions.reason: Readable says what letting them go means here: leaving them alone, not punishing them.

records.source: ἐπείσθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ, καὶ προσκαλεσάμενοι τοὺς ἀποστόλους δείραντες παρήγγειλαν μὴ λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἀπέλυσαν.
records.gloss: They were persuaded then by him, \v 40 and having called the apostles, having beaten they commanded not to speak in the name of the Jesus and released [them].
pieces: Gamaliel's words won them over.
They summoned the apostles, had them beaten, and commanded them to stop speaking in the name of Jesus. Then they released them.

L.39: And they were persuaded by him,
L.40: and having called the apostles in, they beat [them] and commanded [them] not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released [them].

R.39: The council members agreed with Gamaliel.
R.40: They called the apostles back in and had them whipped. They ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus anymore. Then they let them go.

decisions.choice: they were persuaded by him: they took his advice not to kill them
alternatives: they were convinced the apostles were right
decisions.reason: They give up the plan to kill (5:33), but still punish the apostles and repeat their order.

decisions.choice: beat them: likely the Jewish penalty of lashes
decisions.reason: The verb means to beat or flog. The law allowed up to forty lashes (Deuteronomy 25:2-3), and Paul says he received "forty lashes less one" five times (2 Corinthians 11:24). Jesus had warned that his followers would be beaten (Mark 13:9).

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus: by Jesus's authority, as his messengers
decisions.reason: As in 4:17-18, where they were told not to speak or teach in this name.

decisions.choice: had them whipped
decisions.reason: Readable names the most likely form of the beating, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἐπορεύοντο χαίροντες ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ συνεδρίου ὅτι κατηξιώθησαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος ἀτιμασθῆναι·
records.gloss: They indeed therefore were going rejoicing from presence of the council, because they were counted worthy for the name to be dishonored.
pieces: As they went out from the council, the apostles were glad: they had been found worthy to bear shame for the sake of the Name.

L.41: So they went out from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to be dishonored for the sake of the Name.

R.41: The apostles left the council meeting full of joy. God had counted them worthy to suffer shame because they belonged to Jesus.

decisions.choice: rejoicing in disgrace: as Jesus told them
decisions.reason: Jesus said, "Blessed are you when people hate you ... because of the Son of Man. Rejoice in that day" (Luke 6:22-23).

decisions.choice: counted worthy: by God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the one who counts unnamed. It is God who honors them, while the council shames them: worthy to be dishonored.

decisions.choice: the Name: the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: The name of Jesus, spoken of alone as a title (3 John 7). The council had forbidden them to speak in it (5:40).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the Name"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "his name" or "the name of Jesus"
decisions.reason: Later manuscripts fill out the phrase in several ways; the King James Version has "his name". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: because they belonged to Jesus
alternatives: for the sake of the Name
decisions.reason: Readable says what suffering for the Name means: they suffered because they were Jesus's own and spoke for him.

decisions.choice: the apostles
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name them.

records.source: πᾶσάν τε ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ κατ’ οἶκον οὐκ ἐπαύοντο διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.
records.gloss: Every then day in the temple and by house not they were ceasing teaching and proclaiming good news the Christ Jesus.
pieces: Every day, both in the temple and in people's homes, they went on teaching without a break, and announcing the good news that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is Jesus.

L.42: And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming the good news that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [is] Jesus.

R.42: Every day the apostles taught in the temple courts and in people's homes. They never stopped telling the good news that Jesus is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: proclaiming the Christ, Jesus: that the Messiah is Jesus
alternatives: proclaiming Christ Jesus as a name
decisions.reason: With the article, "the Christ" is the title: the Messiah Israel awaited. The message is that he is Jesus, as in 17:3 and 18:5, 18:28. It is not yet used here as a name.

decisions.choice: proclaiming the good news: announcing good news
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for good news. Luke uses it often for telling the message of Jesus (8:4, 8:35).

decisions.choice: from house to house: in homes as well as the temple
decisions.reason: As in 2:46. They obey God rather than the council (5:29).

decisions.choice: the Christ is Jesus (B); Jesus is the Christ (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Greek order, which makes "the Christ" plainly a title; Readable uses the usual English order for the same statement.
